rain. Between 3 and 5 inches of rain have fallen. The expected
rainfall rate is 2 to 3 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall

rainfall. Flash flooding is already occurring.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Area, Central Southwest, Willowbend, northern Riverstone, Alief,

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 23 at 5:00PM MDT until July 23 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 500 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain have moved across the Middle and South Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Up
to 0.7 inches of rain have fallen in the Muddy Creek Basin with up to
a half inch falling across a larger portion of the southern Aspen
Acres Burn scars. Flooding impacts will continue until the water has
a chance to recede. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris
flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other
loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Middle and South Aspen
Acres Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle and South Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rye, San Isabel, Beulah and Colorado City.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Saint Charles River, Muddy Creek and its tributaries, Spring Branch
and South Creek and its tributaries.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Middle and South Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Severe debris flows
can also be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be
washed away in places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to
safety.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 23 at 3:56PM MST until July 27 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 105 to
119 degrees. Major to Extreme Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Arizona and southeast California.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST /8 PM PDT/ Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 23 at 3:51PM PDT until July 23 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 649 North and Central
Coastal Strip, Fire Weather Zone 650 North Coastal Lowlands,
Fire Weather Zone 651 Central Coastal Lowlands, Fire Weather
Zone 652 West Portion of the Olympic Mountains, Fire Weather
Zone 655 Black Hills and Southwest Interior Lowlands, Fire
Weather Zone 659 West Slopes of the Central Cascades Generally
above 1500 Feet and Fire Weather Zone 661 East Portion of the
Olympic Mountains.

* WINDS...West 5 to 10 mph with gusts to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 50 percent.

* LIGHTNING...Isolated thunderstorm coverage is possible across
the southern Cascade Mountains and portions of southwest
Washington. Thunderstorms will develop late Wednesday night
and move from south to north across the area.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Any storms that develop will be capable of
gusty and erratic outflow winds between 25 and 30 miles per
hour. Outflow winds can occur ahead of and behind storms and
cause erratic wind directions.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 77.

* IMPACTS...Scattered lightning in dry fuels can cause multiple
fire starts. Thunderstorms can also bring sudden sharp wind
shifts on existing fires, causing rapid changes in a fire's
rate of spread and direction of spread. Thunderstorm outflow
winds can be a threat for several hours following the start of
a new lightning-caused fire. If a fire were to begin, air
quality may diminish in the surrounding area.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either imminent or occurring now. Any fires that develop will
likely spread quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 23 at 3:33PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology and the Benton Clean Air
Agency have issued an Air Quality Alert until 9 AM PDT Friday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Alert, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.


Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.
Information from the Benton County Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.bentoncleanair.org or call 509-783-1304.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Talkeetna River at the Talkeetna Railroad Bridge and
Upstream of Talkeetna, in addition to the Susitna River near
Sunshine.

* WHEN...Until 315 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Water over roadways.
River or stream flows are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
-
At 200 PM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the advisory area. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly, especially
near Talkeetna River at the Talkeetna Railroad Bridge.
Between 3.5 and 4.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts of 0.1 to 0.3 inches are possible.
-
Rainfall will move out of the advisory area this afternoon.
However, drainage from prior heavy rainfall will continue to
cause flooding through this evening.
-
For Susitna River near Sunshine:
At 12:00pm the stage was 21.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 24.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 22.5 feet is expected around 10:00am
Friday.

For Talkeetna River Upstream of Talkeetna:
At 12:45pm the stage was 11.6 feet.
Flood Stage is 12.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 12.3 feet is expected around 10:00pm
Thursday.
-
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Thursday July 23 to 400 PM Friday July 24

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Ozone will remain in the Good to Moderate
range on Thursday. On Friday, hot and sunny weather will allow
Ozone to reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category.  For
Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Friday, July 24, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone pollution
through state policies. For more information about health impacts
and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Mecklenburg, NC; Union, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 5:40PM EDT until July 23 at 9:45PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Nuisance flooding caused by excessive rainfall may be
ongoing.

* WHERE...Southeastern Mecklenburg County in the piedmont of North
Carolina...
Northern Union NC County in the piedmont of North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.
A few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 539 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicate
earlier heavy rain across the Goose Creek and Crooked Creek
watersheds has ended.  Light showers persist across the Advisory
area, but these showers will not exacerbate ongoing excessive
runoff and stream rises. However, North Fork Crooked Creek and
South Fork Crooked Creek continue to rise with bankfull
conditions possible over the next 1-2 hours before these streams
crest.  Therefore, the Flood Advisory will remain in effect
through at least 9pm to allow streams to crest and conditions to
improve. Isolated areas of nuisance flooding may be ongoing in
areas from Matthews to Indian Trail to Hemby Bridge, especially
adjacent to the north and south forks of Crooked Creek.

- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms are expected to
develop through the early overnight in the vicinity of the
current Advisory area.  These showers and storms will be very
efficient at producing brief periods of heavy rainfall. Where
earlier heavy rainfall has occurred, soils are saturated and
streams are elevated.  Therefore, additional heavy rain may
quickly create new areas of flooding and cause previous areas of
flooding to redevelop.  Caution is advised near any stream or
other vulnerable area.  Stay weather aware through this evening
and have multiple ways to receive Advisories and Warnings.

- Some locations that may experience nuisance floodinginclude...
Matthews, Indian Trail, Unionville, and Hemby Bridge.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued July 23 at 4:15PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

**Bertha expected to weaken as it moves through Southeast Texas**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Brazoria Islands, Chambers, Coastal Brazoria, Coastal
Galveston, and Galveston Island

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 40 miles north of Galveston TX
- 29.8N 94.7W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 290 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha is currently moving westward through southeast
Texas, roughtly around the I-10 corridor nearly Galveston bay. It's
intensity has decreased, with peak winds upwards of 35 knots. Bertha
will continue to weaken, becoming a post-tropical system as it moves
westward tonight. No significant impacts to Southeast Texas are
expected at this time. Winds of 15-25 knots with gusts to 35 knots will
be possible, mainly along the coast and Gulf waters. Scattered showers
and thunderstorms continue this evening. Heavy downpours are possible
though the flooding rain threat is very low. A high risk rip currents
will continue across the beaches and coast through Friday.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Southeast Texas. Remain well sheltered from hazardous wind having
possible limited impacts. If realized, these impacts
include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
the Southeast Texas coast. Remain well guarded against locally
hazardous flood waters having possible  limited
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:
There will be a high risk of rip currents across the upper Texas
coastal beaches through Friday.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 7 PM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued July 23 at 3:55PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**TROPICAL STORM BERTHA HAS MOVED INLAND INTO SOUTHEASTERN TEXAS.**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Tropical Storm Warning has been cancelled for Lower Iberia,
Lower St. Mary, and Lower Vermilion

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for East Cameron, Lower
Jefferson, and West Cameron

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 30 miles northwest of High Island TX or about 80 miles
west of Cameron LA
- 29.8N 94.7W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 290 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha has moved inland over lower Southeast Texas
continuing a weakening trend. Tropical storm warnings have been
discontinued east of the Cameron / Vermilion Parish line as well as
marine south extending south and east of Calcasieu Pass. Tropical
Storm Warnings remain in effect across western Cameron Parish,
Louisiana, and Jefferson County, Texas including Calcasieu and Sabine
Lakes. The remainder of the forecast remains unchanged with 1 to
2 feet of surge possible and most of the heavy rainfall remaining
offshore due to the sheared nature of the convection. Bertha is
expected to weaken into a tropical depression overnight as it
encounters more land interaction moving further into Texas.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Southwest Louisiana / Southeast Texas. Remain well sheltered from hazardous
wind having limited impacts. If realized,
these impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding across
Southwest Louisiana / Southeast Texas. Remain well away from locally hazardous
surge having limited impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:

Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

During the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your
shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the best
foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the weather.

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.



* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Lake Charles LA around 10 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 4:47PM EDT until July 24 at 4:45AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Rowan County in the piedmont of North
Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 445 AM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
River or stream flows are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 438 PM EDT, Storm totals rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches
caused streams in the Second Creek watershed to rise above
bankfull. While tributaries have crested and receded below
bankfull, the stream gauge on Second Creek near US-70 shows
Second Creek remains above action stage. Therefore, nuisance
flooding of adjacent low-lying areas is on going and will
continue for the next several hours.
- No additional heavy rainfall is expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Piedmont Research Station.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Only when it is safe to do so, please report flooding or landslides
threatening roads or property to the National Weather Service
Greenville-Spartanburg by calling 1...800...2 6 7...8 1 0 1, by
posting on our Facebook page, or by posting on X using hashtag
NWSGSP. Your message should describe the specific location, address,
or intersection where impacts occurred and the depth of flooding
observed.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 445 AM EDT FRIDAY

properties.description:
...SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ON THURSDAY ACROSS FAR EASTERN OREGON
AND WESTERN IDAHO...
...HOT, DRY, AND WINDY FRIDAY AND SATURDAY...

.Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop across far
eastern Oregon and western Idaho this afternoon. Storms will be
capable of frequent lightning, gusty outflow winds, and only
sporadic wetting rains. While the thunderstorm threat will end by
Friday and Saturday, hot, dry, and windy conditions will develop,
primarily across southeast Oregon and the higher terrain of
southwest Idaho. The driest and windiest day at this time is
expected on Saturday.

...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 2 PM MDT /1 PM PDT/ FRIDAY TO
9 PM MDT /8 PM PDT/ SATURDAY FOR WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE
HUMIDITIES FOR OWYHEE MOUNTAINS...SOUTHERN GRASSLANDS...CENTRAL
CANYONLANDS...NORTHWESTERN VALE BLM AND BAKER VALLEY...WHICH ARE
FIRE WEATHER ZONES 423...672...673...674 AND 675...

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Red Flag
Warning for winds and low relative humidities, which is in effect
from 2 PM MDT /1 PM PDT/ Friday to 9 PM MDT /8 PM PDT/ Saturday.
The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in effect.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Idaho, Fire Weather Zone 423 Owyhee
Mountains. In Oregon, Fire Weather Zones 672 Southern
Grasslands, 673 Central Canyonlands, 674 Northwestern Vale BLM
and 675 Baker Valley.

* TIMING...For the first Red Flag Warning, until 9 PM MDT /8 PM
PDT/ this evening. For the second Red Flag Warning, from 2 PM
MDT /1 PM PDT/ Friday to 9 PM MDT /8 PM PDT/ Saturday.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Scattered coverage with abundant lightning.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty erratic winds up to 50 mph.

* WINDS...For the second Red Flag Warning, Southwest 10 to 20 mph
with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...For the second Red Flag Warning, 6 to 12
percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will occur shortly.

properties.areaDesc: Central Brooks Range; Romanzof Mountains
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 23 at 11:46AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A cold front is currently moving northwest to southeast across
the North Slope. As the front reaches the Brooks Range,
precipitation begins as rain then transitions to a mix this
afternoon/evening. There is uncertainty with exact precipitation
types, but Anaktuvuk Pass should mix with snow and freezing
drizzle between 3 PM and 5 PM resulting in a glaze of ice on
elevated surfaces as temperatures drop near freezing this evening.
Atigun Pass should transition to all snow by 4 PM with snow
accumulations around a few inches. With rain and surface
temperatures above freezing to start the event, snow is not
expected to stick to the road immediately. With any heavier rates
tonight, some slushy accumulations are possible. As the snow ends
tonight, temperatures plummet into the 20s which could result in
patches of ice by Friday morning. Any patches of ice will melt by
the early afternoon as temperatures rise above freezing.

NWSheadline: Rain Transitions to a Mix of This Afternoon and Evening

properties.areaDesc: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast; Central Arctic Plains
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 23 at 11:46AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A front moving across the Arctic Coast today will bring rain
showers which transition to a wintry mix this evening. The chances
for a wintry mix increase from 5PM to 11PM tonight. This wintry
mix can be sleet, snow and freezing drizzle. After midnight
Thursday night, the steadiest and heaviest precipitation should
transition to a mist or freezing drizzle which can result in
patchy ice, especially on colder/elevated surfaces. Otherwise,
Friday will be chilly with patchy ice possible in the morning. If
there is any ice, it will melt by the late morning on Friday.

NWSheadline: Rain Transitions to a Wintry Mix This Evening and Tonight

properties.areaDesc: Grande Ronde Valley of Oregon; Eagle Cap Wilderness; Western Forested Blue Mountains
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 23 at 12:25PM PDT until July 23 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
...HIGH ABUNDANT LIGHTNING RISK WITH THUNDERSTORMS TODAY... ...
WINDY AND BREEZY WITH CRITICAL RH FRIDAY AND SATURDAY...

The upper level low offshore will shift to the east just enough
to allow for monsoonal moisture to move into the region.
Instability will accompany the moisture and allow for increased
chances of isolated to scattered thunderstorms across the eastern
mountains. Brief heavy downpours, gusty outflow winds in excess
of 45 mph, small hail, and frequent lightning will be possible. A
strong to briefly severe thunderstorm cannot be ruled out this
afternoon and early evening.

Friday the upper level low will eject into the region bringing
windy conditions to many of the Cascade Gaps as well as central
OR. Humidities both Friday and Saturday will be critical.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 694 Grande Ronde Valley of
Oregon, 695 Eagle Cap Wilderness and 699 Western Forested Blue
Mountains.

* TIMING...Until 8 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Isolated to scattered dry thunderstorms
Thursday after 1200.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusts from 25-45 mph
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with temperatures of 100 to 105

* WHERE...Eastern Cochise County below 5000 feet, Upper San Pedro
River Valley, and Upper Santa Cruz River Valley/Altar Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 8 PM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Asherton affecting Dimmit County.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until early Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 29.0 feet, Widespread major flooding threatens
livestock over a large area of the flood plain. A mile of Farm to
Market 190 near the river is flooded and flow is within a foot of
the Farm to Market 190 bridge floor over the Nueces River. The
Nueces River and Turkey Creek are a mile and a half wide south and
west of Carrizo Springs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 28.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 1:30 PM CDT Thursday was 29.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
early Sunday morning and continue falling to 10.4 feet early
Tuesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
28.6 feet on 07/17/1990.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning by 815 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 23 at 1:49PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

For the Nueces River...including Three Rivers...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...From Monday evening until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 35.0 feet, Major lowland flooding occurs. Flow backs
up minor creeks to the slabs of lowest homes in the River Creek
Acres Subdivision, five miles southeast of George West, requiring
evacuations. Livestock are cut off and could drown in low areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 1.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Monday
evening and continue rising to 35.5 feet early Tuesday afternoon.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.description:

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...Mostly the Shasta and Scott valleys of Fire
Weather Zones 280 and 281, but also portions of the Klamath
National Forest.

* WINDS...Southwest to west 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* MINIMUM HUMIDITY...10 to 15 percent.

* DURATION...3 to 7 hours Friday afternoon.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. You can find your county's
emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Be sure you're signed up for your county's emergency alert
system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 23 at 11:11AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued an
Ozone (OZ) High Pollution Advisory for the Tucson Metro area
Friday morning through Friday evening.

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute, or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/tucson or call 602-771-2300.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued July 23 at 10:10AM PDT until July 26 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH IN EFFECT FROM SUNDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH
SUNDAY EVENING FOR GUSTY WINDS AND LOW HUMIDITY FOR PORTIONS OF
NORTHEAST CA AND WESTERN NV...

The National Weather Service in Reno has issued a Red Flag
Warning for gusty winds and low humidity, which is in effect from
1 PM Friday to 9 PM PDT Saturday. A Fire Weather Watch has also
been issued. This Fire Weather Watch for gusty winds and low
humidity is in effect from Sunday afternoon through Sunday
evening. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in effect.

* CHANGES...Upgraded Friday and Saturday to a Red Flag Warning.
Also issued a Fire Weather Watch for Sunday.

* Affected Area...Fire Weather Zone 270 Surprise Valley
California, Fire Weather Zone 278 Eastern Lassen County, Fire
Weather Zone 458 Northern Washoe County.

* Winds...Southwest 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph each
afternoon.

* Humidity...Afternoon minimums 5 to 9 percent Friday through
Sunday.

* Duration...3 to 9 hours Friday and Saturday afternoon. 3 to 6
hours Sunday afternoon.

* Impacts...The combination of gusty winds and low humidity can
cause fire to rapidly grow in size and intensity before first
responders can contain them.
properties.instruction:
Avoid outdoor activities that can cause a spark near dry
vegetation, such as yard work, target shooting, or campfires.
Follow local fire restrictions. Check weather.gov/reno for
updates and livingwithfire.info for preparedness tips.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Piedmont and western North Carolina, including
the following areas, in Piedmont North Carolina, Cabarrus, Catawba,
Cleveland, Davie, Gaston, Iredell, Lincoln, Mecklenburg and Rowan.
In western North Carolina, Buncombe, Burke Mountains, Eastern

Haywood, Henderson, Macon, Madison, McDowell Mountains, Mitchell,

Jackson, Swain, Transylvania and Yancey.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

continue moving along a slow-moving cold front through this
afternoon. While additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
expected to be widespread across the watch area this afternoon,
isolated locations are expected to see multiple rounds of very
heavy rainfall, and localized amounts as high as 3 inches are
possible, enhancing the potential for flash flooding in these
areas.

onset flooding based on current forecasts. Flash flooding is a very
dangerous situation and may impact areas that do not typically flood.

quickly should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 23 at 9:18AM PDT until July 24 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING FOR THUNDERSTORMS THURSDAY, FIRE WEATHER
WATCHES FOR WINDS AND LOW HUMIDITY FRIDAY AND SATURDAY...

A ridge breakdown will first bring a threat for thunderstorms
across portions of central and north-central Washington today and
tonight. Drier weather arrives Friday and Saturday, though winds
will become increasingly gusty with critical fire weather
conditions likely.

* Affected Area: Okanogan Valley (Zone 703) and Foothills of
Central Washington Cascades (Zone 705).

* Lightning: 15 to 30 percent chance of thunderstorms through 2 AM
Friday. Gusty and erratic outflow winds up to 35 mph possible in
any thunderstorms.

* Winds: Friday afternoon winds - West/Southwest 10 to 20 mph with
gusts up to 30 mph. Saturday afternoon winds - West/Southwest
winds 15 to 30 mph with gusts around 30 to 40 mph.

* Relative Humidities: 11 to 25 percent.

* Impacts: New fire starts from lightning Thursday. New and
existing fires could be impacted by gusty outflow winds. Gusty
winds and low humidity Friday and Saturday afternoon may lead
to rapid fire spread with any new or ongoing fires.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.areaDesc: Maricopa, AZ
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 23 at 9:15AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has extended
an Ozone High Pollution Advisory for the Phoenix Metro Area through
Friday.

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot daytime conditions with high temperatures between 100
and 108 common. Warm overnight conditions will bring less relief
than usual.

* WHERE...Antelope Valley.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for dangerous heat illness,
especially for sensitive groups like the very young, the very old,
those without air conditioning, and those active outdoors.
properties.instruction:

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Do not leave young
children and pets in unattended vehicles. Limit strenuous activities
to early morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of
heat exhaustion and heat stroke.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued July 23 at 10:36AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

**Disorganized Bertha Approaching Southeast Texas**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Brazoria Islands, Chambers, Coastal Brazoria, Coastal
Galveston, and Galveston Island

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 100 miles east-northeast of Galveston TX
- 29.6N 93.2W
- Storm Intensity 45 mph
- Movement West or 275 degrees at 10 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

At 10 AM CDT, Tropical Storm Bertha was located along the western
Louisiana coastline as poorly organized and very asymetrical tropical
system. Bertha is still expected to continue moving westward through
an unfavorable environment with high wind shear, dry air, and land
interaction. Bertha is still expected to reach the upper Texas coast
this afternoon as a weak Tropical Storm or Tropical Depression. No
significant impacts to Southeast Texas are expected at this time.
Winds of 20-25 knots with gusts to 40 knots will be possible, mainly along
the coast and Gulf waters throughout today. Scattered showers and
thunderstorms are possible, and could produce locally heavy rainfall
in spots, though the flooding rain threat remains low. There will be a high
risk rip currents across the beaches and coast through Friday.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
Southeast Texas. Potential impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across the Southeast Texas coast. Potential
impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:
There will be a high risk of rip currents across the upper Texas
coastal beaches through Friday.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 4 PM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**TROPICAL STORM BERTHA TRACKING WEST ALONG THE SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA COAST.**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for East Cameron, Lower
Iberia, Lower Jefferson, Lower St. Mary, Lower Vermilion, and
West Cameron

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 70 miles east of High Island TX or about 120 miles west
of Morgan City LA
- 29.6N 93.2W
- Storm Intensity 45 mph
- Movement West or 275 degrees at 10 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Bertha continues to maintain tropical storm force winds, albeit mostly
over the Gulf waters tracking west below Cameron Parish. The storm is
moving due west and will move along the coast or into southeast Texas
tonight. Tropical storm warnings are in effect from Morgan City along
the Louisiana coastline into coastal Southeast Texas. The remainder of
the forecast remains mostly unchanged with 1 to 2 feet of surge
possible and most of the heavy rainfall remaining offshore due to the
sheared nature of the convection.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
coastal portions of Louisiana. Remain well sheltered from hazardous
wind having limited impacts. If realized,
these impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding across
immediate coastline. Remain well away from locally hazardous
surge having limited impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:

Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

During the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your
shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the best
foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the weather.

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org

surf elevated beyond Friday, which may require the advisory to be
extended through the weekend.

* WHERE...South facing shores of all Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...From 6 AM this morning to 6 AM HST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.

go out.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 23 at 2:47AM PDT until July 27 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected. Afternoon temperatures
in the desert valleys will climb into the 108 to 114 degree range,
and may exceed 115 along the Colorado River Valley and 120 in Death
Valley. Overnight lows generally 80 to 95 degrees.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada including the Greater Mojave Desert region.

* WHEN...From 10 AM PDT /10 AM MST/ this morning to 8 PM PDT /8 PM
MST/ Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.areaDesc: Grand Canyon Country
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 23 at 1:45AM MST until July 26 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected below 4000 feet, with
daytime temperatures around 105 degrees at Havasupai Gardens, and
112 to 114 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 8 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This warning is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures are expected to rise to dangerous levels.

Day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1 1/2
miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

Hike smart.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM FRIDAY TO 8 PM MST SUNDAY BELOW 4000 FEET

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued July 23 at 3:47AM EDT until July 25 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3
to 7 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Walton, Bay, and Gulf County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT /7 PM CDT/
this evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late
Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Pinellas, Coastal Hillsborough, Coastal Manatee,
Coastal Sarasota, Coastal Charlotte and Coastal Lee Counties.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Columbia River Gorge of Oregon; Lower Columbia Basin of Oregon; Foothills of the Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon; Eastern Columbia River Gorge of Washington; Yakima Valley; Lower Columbia Basin of Washington; Foothills of the Blue Mountains of Washington
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 22 at 11:17PM PDT until July 23 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with temperatures up to 103 degrees. This
will pose a moderate to major risk of heat-related illness.

* WHERE...Eastern Columbia River Gorge of Oregon and Washington,
Lower Columbia Basin of Oregon and Washington, Foothills of the
Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon, Yakima Valley, and Foothills of
the Blue Mountains of Washington.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible.
To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

For sheltering information and other human services in your area,
dial 2 1 1 during business hours or visit 211info.org for Oregon or
wa211.org for Washington anytime.

properties.instruction:
A Heat Advisory means that hot weather conditions are occurring or
expected. This will create a situation in which heat illnesses are
possible.

even for a few minutes. Car interiors can reach lethal temperatures
in a matter of minutes.

Stay indoors and seek air-conditioned buildings. Drink water more
than usual, and avoid dehydrating alcoholic, sugary, or caffeinated
drinks. Dress for the heat by wearing lightweight and light colored
clothing. Eat small meals and eat more often. Monitor those with a
higher vulnerability to heat, including small children. Check in on
family, friends, and neighbors, especially the elderly. If engaging
in outdoor activity, take longer and more frequent breaks and avoid
the hottest parts of the day.

properties.areaDesc: San Bernardino and Riverside County Valleys-The Inland Empire; San Bernardino County Mountains; Coachella Valley; San Gorgonio Pass Near Banning; Orange County Inland
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 5:41PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the South Coast Air Basin and Coachella Valley. Levels
of ozone pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...until 8 PM Monday. The highest ozone levels typically occur
in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours
* Try to delay trips to the gas station and the use of household
chemicals until the evening
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued July 22 at 8:08PM EDT until July 25 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northeast, and northwest
Georgia, including the following counties, in north central
Georgia, Cherokee, Dawson, Fannin, Forsyth, Gilmer, Hall, Lumpkin,
Pickens and Union. In northeast Georgia, Banks, Towns and White. In
northwest Georgia, Bartow, Catoosa, Chattooga, Dade, Floyd, Gordon,
Murray, Polk, Walker and Whitfield.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Repeated rounds of rainfall along a stalled frontal boundary are
likely through late week. An anomalously moist environment over
Georgia will support high rain rates and increased chances for
flash flooding. Widespread rainfall of 2 to 4 inches will be
possible with locally higher amounts of 5 inches or more. Urban
areas, and areas with poor drainage, will be the most susceptible
to flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
Water levels will rise slightly with each high tide Wednesday

be in Eastern Norton Sound, around 1 to 3 feet above the normal
high tide line. Water level rises around 0.5 to 1.5 feet are
expected from Golovin to Nome.

NWSheadline: Minor Water Level Rises Wednesday Night Through Friday Morning

properties.areaDesc: Central Brooks Range
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 2:11PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
An Arctic cold front extending from the high arctic will move
southeast towards mainland Alaska. This front will likely bring
chances of precipitation along higher terrain beginning Thursday.
Current model guidance supports the possibility of light rain
Friday morning, with a transition to snow expected towards the
evening and overnight hours. Storm total snowfall accumulations
could be 3 to 5 inches, however with surface temperatures above
freezing, the snow is not anticipated to stick to the road. If the
roads remain wet overnight Friday then there could be patches of
ice, due to air temperatures dipping into the 20s above.

NWSheadline: RAIN/SNOW MIX POSSIBLE IN THE CENTRAL BROOKS RANGE THURSDAY THROUGH FRIDAY MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Hatcher Pass; Western Susitna Valley; Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley; Northern Susitna Valley
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued July 22 at 1:23PM AKDT until July 23 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Susitna Valley and Hatcher Pass. This
includes the cities of Skwentna, Willow, Talkeetna, Trapper Creek,
Petersville, and Chulitna.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water
crossings may be flooded. Area rivers, creeks, and streams are
elevated from the previous rain event and will likely rise again
over the next 24 hours.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A storm moving in today will bring an additional 1 to 2.5
inches of rain to the Susitna Valley and Hatcher Pass. As a
result, fast responding rivers and streams along and east of
the Parks Highway may be more susceptible to flooding with
this event.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH THURSDAY AFTERNOON

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 8:53AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued an
Ozone High Pollution Advisory for the Phoenix Metro Area on
Thursday.

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.
